articles.title: Câmeras não mostram saída de mulher que desapareceu de hospital no PR | G1
articles.standfirst: Paciente foi encontrada em um terminal de Pinhais, na Grande Curitiba. Família diz que câmeras do hospital não registraram a saída dela.
articles.summary: Paciente foi encontrada em um terminal de Pinhais, na Grande Curitiba. Família diz que câmeras do hospital não registraram a saída dela.
articles.body:
Roseli Mendes, de 60 anos, que desapareceu enquanto estava internada no Hospital Santa Casa, em Curitiba , saiu da unidade com o acesso venoso, usando a pulseira de identificação e percorreu cerca de 11 km de ônibus até ser encontrada em um terminal de Pinhais , na Região Metropolitana de Curitiba (RMC). Entenda mais abaixo.

Segundo a filha, Camila Mendes, a família teve acesso às imagens das câmeras de segurança do hospital, mas não conseguiu identificar Roseli deixando a unidade.

"É muito estranho passar com acesso venoso e pulseiras no braço. Foram abertas as câmeras com um familiar junto, mas não mostrou nada em nenhum momento", contou Camila.

Roseli faz tratamento contra um câncer e foi internada na Santa Casa na terça-feira (27), por volta das 18h, após apresentar um quadro de inflamação no pulmão. Na manhã de quarta-feira (28), quando a filha voltou ao hospital para levar roupas e objetos pessoais, a paciente não estava mais no quarto.

Segundo relatos de outras pacientes que dividiam o quarto com Roseli, ela havia dito que iria embora e saiu do local.

A paciente havia passado por uma sessão de radioterapia cerca de dez dias antes de desaparecer. Segundo a filha, desde domingo (25), ela apresentava sinais de alucinações.

Roseli foi encontrada em um ônibus, na Região Metropolitana de Curitiba — Foto: Reprodução

A família passou a procurar Roseli nas imediações do hospital e em outros pontos da cidade. Camila também foi a uma delegacia e ao Instituto Médico-Legal (IML), mas não conseguiu informações sobre o paradeiro da mãe.

Por volta das 23h de quarta-feira, Roseli foi encontrada em um terminal de ônibus em Pinhais. Uma mulher que tinha assistido à reportagem da RPC , afiliada da TV Globo no Paraná , reconheceu a paciente e acionou a polícia.

Após ser encontrada, Roseli voltou à Santa Casa, onde permanece em segurança, recebendo atendimento médico e sendo monitorada. Segundo Camila, a equipe médica deve realizar exames para investigar o quadro de saúde da paciente.

“Foi um desespero, muito angustiante. Eu fiquei o tempo todo aqui no hospital esperando notícias. Ela ainda está meio perdida, viveu um momento estranho, mas está desorientada e cansada. Vão fazer exames para ver”, relatou.

Como mulher reconheceu paciente no ônibus

Patrícia de Goes estava dentro de um ônibus a caminho do trabalho quando percebeu que uma passageira parecia familiar. Uma amiga comentou que tinha visto Roseli na televisão , e as duas procuraram a reportagem na internet.

Segundo Patrícia, o motorista também chamou a atenção das passageiras porque aquela era a segunda volta que Roseli dava com ele na mesma linha.

Roseli foi reconhecida por Patrícia depois que a notícia do desaparecimento foi transmitida na RPC — Foto: Reprodução

Segundo Patrícia, quando foi encontrada, Roseli estava calma, mas desorientada. Ela tentava ir para casa, que fica em Colombo , também na Região Metropolitana de Curitiba.

"Ela queria ir para casa da filha. Ela falava: 'É aqui o ônibus que eu vou para casa da minha filha? Eu vou ficar aqui sentadinha e vocês falam para eu descer [...] Eu estou grata porque ela está bem hoje. Eu fiquei preocupada. Vai saber o que ia acontecer com essa senhora", disse Patrícia.

Em nota divulgada nesta quinta-feira (29), o Hospital Santa Casa de Curitiba comemorou o reencontro e informou que continua apurando as circunstâncias do caso em conjunto com as autoridades. Leia na íntegra:

"A ISCMC e a Santa Casa de Curitiba ficaram felizes com o desfecho positivo do reencontro da paciente. Desde os primeiros momentos de ontem, não deixaram de se esmerar na busca, no fornecimento de amparo aos familiares, na análise da situação e na prestação de informações aos envolvidos e, principalmente, às autoridades. Hoje, 29/10/2026, a paciente encontra-se em segurança na instituição, recebendo atendimento médico e sendo monitorada. Continuamos com os procedimentos de verificação e apuração no hospital, em conjunto com as autoridades".

articles.title: Jovem em remissão de câncer ganha vídeo surpresa de Neymar | G1
articles.standfirst: Adolescente de Jaguariúna recebeu camisa autografada, vídeo e cadeira gamer do ídolo; família de Eduardo Ribeiro Melo, de 16 anos, agora busca apoio para participar de tratamento que pode reduzir o risco de recidiva da doença.
articles.summary: Adolescente de Jaguariúna recebeu camisa autografada, vídeo e cadeira gamer do ídolo; família agora busca apoio para participar de tratamento nos Estados Unidos.
articles.body:
Torcedor do Palmeiras, mas fã declarado de Neymar, o estudante Eduardo Ribeiro Melo, de 16 anos, de Jaguariúna (SP), viveu um dia que dificilmente vai esquecer. Em remissão após enfrentar um osteossarcoma, um tipo de câncer que afeta os ossos, o jovem ganhou um computador gamer, visitou o estádio do time do coração e ainda recebeu uma camisa autografada e uma mensagem em vídeo do ídolo.

Agora, enquanto comemora o fim do tratamento, se prepara para uma nova etapa: participar de um tratamento nos Estados Unidos que pode reduzir o risco de retorno da doença. Entenda mais abaixo.

As homenagens fizeram parte da realização de um sonho promovida pela ONG Make-A-Wish ("Faça um Desejo"), que atende crianças e adolescentes com doenças graves.

O desejo de Eduardo era simples: ter um computador gamer. O que ele não imaginava era que a experiência envolveria justamente o seu maior ídolo.

"Ele é palmeirense, mas sempre gostou muito do Neymar. Quando recebeu tudo isso, ficou encantado. Foi algo totalmente inesperado", conta a mãe, Tathiane Melo, de 45 anos.

A entrega dos presentes ocorreu em 18 de outubro, durante um encontro com voluntários da instituição em São Paulo. Além do computador, Eduardo recebeu uma camisa autografada por Neymar, assistiu a uma mensagem gravada pelo atleta especialmente para ele e participou de um passeio pelo estádio do Palmeiras.

Segundo a mãe, a ligação do adolescente com o craque surgiu durante as conversas com os voluntários da ONG. Antes de realizar cada sonho, a equipe procura conhecer melhor a criança ou adolescente atendido, fazendo perguntas sobre hobbies, preferências e ídolos.

"Quando eles descobriram que o Eduardo era fã do Neymar, começaram a planejar tudo. Até brincavam que ele era palmeirense, mas tinha como ídolo um jogador identificado com o Santos", relembra Tathiane.

Nesta quinta-feira (29), o jovem recebeu em casa mais uma surpresa: a cadeira gamer enviada pelo ídolo. "Foi muito legal. Eu realmente não esperava por tudo isso", resumiu o adolescente.

Em tratamento de um osteossarcoma, um tipo de câncer que afeta os ossos, Eduardo Ribeiro Melo, de 16 anos, visitou o estádio do time do coração, mas foi surpreendido com presentes do ídolo Neymar: uma camisa autografada, uma mensagem em vídeo e a cadeira gamer enviada pelo craque — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

As surpresas chegaram após um período desafiador para a família. Em julho de 2025, quando tinha 15 anos, Eduardo recebeu o diagnóstico de osteossarcoma . O tratamento foi realizado no Hospital Boldrini, em Campinas .

"Depois desse diagnóstico, eu fui pro Hospital Boldrini, fazer o tratamento todo. Dia 2 de dezembro, eu fiz a retirada da fíbula, onde estava o tumor. E graças a Deus tudo deu certo", disse o jovem.

Ao longo dos meses seguintes, enfrentou sessões de quimioterapia e os efeitos colaterais do tratamento.

"Foi muito difícil. Teve vômitos, indisposição e momentos de medo e angústia. Mas ele sempre foi muito forte e nunca desistiu", afirma a mãe.

O tratamento foi concluído em setembro de 2025, e o adolescente entrou em remissão da doença.

Mesmo durante o tratamento, Eduardo manteve a rotina de estudos. No meio das consultas e sessões de quimioterapia, prestou exame e ingressou em um curso técnico de mecânica em Amparo (SP).

Hoje, frequenta o ensino médio em Jaguariúna durante o dia e estuda à noite no curso técnico.

Para Tathiane, a trajetória do filho é marcada pela determinação.

"Ele sempre teve muita garra, muita alegria e muita vontade de viver. A gente passou por momentos muito difíceis, mas nunca perdeu a esperança. Graças a Deus, hoje podemos olhar para trás e ver tudo o que ele venceu", diz.

Eduardo Ribeiro Melo, de 16 anos, exibe a cadeira gamer enviada por Neymar, e também um registro da visita com a família ao estádio do Palmeiras, seu time de coração — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Com a doença em remissão, Eduardo e a família se preparam para uma nova fase da jornada contra o câncer.

O adolescente foi aceito em um estudo conduzido pela equipe da médica Giselle Sholler, do Penn State Health, nos Estados Unidos, que busca reduzir as chances de recidiva em pacientes com diferentes tipos de sarcoma.

O contato com o projeto surgiu por meio de outras famílias atendidas pelo Hospital Boldrini, referência no tratamento de câncer infantojuvenil.

Segundo a mãe, Tathiane Melo, o primeiro contato foi feito por e-mail, em 13 de agosto. No mesmo dia, a equipe norte-americana respondeu solicitando o envio de exames e o preenchimento de formulários.

"Na mesma semana fizemos uma chamada de vídeo com a doutora Sholler. Ela explicou como seria o estudo e perguntou se nós queríamos participar. Claro que sim", relembra.

O objetivo é utilizar uma medicação chamada DFMO, que pode ajudar a reduzir o risco de recidiva da doença. Atualmente, mesmo em remissão, Eduardo ainda tem cerca de 20% de chance de o câncer voltar.

"Com essa medicação que ele vai tratar lá, é pra diminuir cada vez mais essa chance. E se Deus quiser até zerar, para nunca mais acontecer de novo", diz a mãe.

A previsão é que o tratamento dure dois anos. Durante esse período, a família precisará viajar aos Estados Unidos cinco vezes para consultas médicas e retirada da medicação.

A primeira viagem já está marcada. Eles embarcam em 16 de novembro, e a consulta inicial está agendada para o dia 18.

A participação no estudo não tem custo, assim como a hospedagem, que será na Casa Ronald McDonald's, mas as despesas com passagens aéreas, que custam cerca de R$ 10 mil para cada um, além de traslados, alimentação e seguros, ficam por conta da família.

Entre as despesas também estão as consultas médicas, avaliadas em US$ 500 a cada visita (cerca de R$ 2,6 mil), além de possíveis exames complementares que venham a ser solicitados pela equipe médica.

"Foi uma coisa que não esperávamos, não nos preparamos para isso", contou Tathiane.

Em tratamento de um osteossarcoma, um tipo de câncer que afeta os ossos, Eduardo Ribeiro Melo, de 16 anos, havia feito um pedido simples para a ONG Make-a-Wish: um computador gamer — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

articles.title: Chili's customers suffer chemical burns after dangerous margarita mix-up
articles.summary: Three customers and two employees suffered symptoms after an industrial degreaser was mistakenly used to prepare margaritas at a North Carolina Chili's.
articles.body: Multiple customers at a Chili's Grill & Bar reported experiencing chemical burns Wednesday after consuming margaritas that had been prepared with an industrial cleaning chemical that was mistaken for sugar or salt. The Foothills Health District said the incident unfolded at a restaurant in Forest City, North Carolina. Three customers consumed the contaminated margaritas, while two restaurant employees also reportedly experienced symptoms after exposure to the chemical, according to the health district. ROACHES CAUGHT CRAWLING ACROSS POPULAR STEAKHOUSE'S KITCHEN FLOOR IN VIRAL EMPLOYEE VIDEO According to preliminary findings, the mix-up began Monday when an employee received an industrial degreaser from a contracted worker and placed it in an unmarked container. The container was then brought inside the restaurant and left in the bar area. Two days later, an employee preparing the bar for lunch service discovered the unlabeled container and, believing its contents to be sugar or salt, used the chemical to prepare the margarita station, the health district said. Shortly after the restaurant opened, three customers consumed the contaminated beverages and "immediately experienced discomfort and chemical burns in and around their mouths." After the customers alerted staff, two employees also tasted the substance and reported similar symptoms. CHILI'S REVIVES ICONIC RED BOOTHS AND CLASSIC DESIGN IN NATIONWIDE RESTAURANT OVERHAUL In a statement to Fox News Digital, Chili's said the company took immediate action to support those affected. "We are aware of an isolated incident at our restaurant in Forest City, North Carolina that resulted in injuries to two of our guests and Team Members. Our team took immediate action to support those affected and avoid any further injuries. We are actively investigating the circumstances related to this incident as the health and wellbeing of our guests and Team Members remain our top priority," the company said. The company’s account differed from the Foothills Health District’s preliminary findings, which said three customers experienced chemical burns after consuming the margaritas. After the Foothills Health District launched an investigation, the restaurant's food service permit was immediately suspended. It was quickly reinstated on Thursday after specialists determined the restaurant met all other food safety standards. MORE THAN 12,000 POUNDS OF BACON RECALLED AFTER USDA ISSUES HIGHEST-RISK ALERT The health district used the incident to remind all food service establishments in North Carolina that chemicals must be properly labeled and stored away from food-handling areas. articles.title: Sudan investigation maps commanders linked to wartime rape
articles.summary: Investigative unit CIR identifies 25 commanders present at five sites during periods of reported sexual violence.
articles.body:
On the day the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) entered el-Fasher in October 2025, a video posted on TikTok showed one of the paramilitary group’s commanders addressing fighters. She appeared to be encouraging fighters to rape women in Sudan’s Northern State, hundreds of kilometres from el-Fasher, the capital of North Darfur.

“The Northern State? You’ll just go for its women, so you cleanse their lineage and bring [brave] sons just like you.”

The speaker was Khademallah Khashmin Herika, also known as Shiraz Khalid, a major commanding the RSF’s female contingent, according to the Centre for Information Resilience (CIR).

The British open-source investigative organisation describes her words as an explicit incitement to rape. It could not establish exactly where the video, posted on October 26, 2025, was filmed. Separate footage placed Herika in el-Fasher and in Garni, where survivors described girls being detained and raped.

Herika is among 25 commanders identified in a CIR investigation into sexual violence in Sudan’s war. Published on Monday, a year after her video was posted, it examines five locations and periods of reported abuse, linking commanders’ appearances and roles to evidence gathered by the United Nations, rights groups and Sudanese organisations.

The findings cover both the RSF and the Sudanese Armed Forces, which have been fighting a three-year-long war, as well as their allied forces. They identify commanders who exercised authority where atrocities were reported, but do not establish that each personally committed or ordered acts of rape.

Investigators checked identities, locations and, where possible, filming dates, with commander sightings independently verified by two analysts. They compared that record with survivor accounts, reported incidents, threatening rhetoric, and indicators of heightened risk, including forced separation of men and women.

The UN fact-finding mission documented mass and gang rape during the RSF takeover of el-Fasher, including at the Saudi Hospital and el-Fasher University. Women and girls were also attacked along escape routes out of the city.

CIR’s report cites a survivor who described being held with other girls at soldiers’ quarters near Garni and raped over two nights. Her family’s detention for ransom further delayed her access to specialist medical care.

The most senior RSF officer identified around el-Fasher was Abdul Rahim Hamdan Dagalo, deputy commander and brother of RSF leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti.

CIR verified him at the army’s former 6th Infantry Division base on October 26, 2025, and at the Saudi Hospital on November 4.

In separate drone footage from October 27, a voice instructs artillery commander Hussein Abu Jalak to pursue vehicles fleeing an earth embankment outside the city, associated with civilian detention and executions. CIR matched the voice to Dagalo by manually comparing it with other verified recordings of him speaking.

RSF sector commander Gedo Hamdan Ahmed, known as Ibn Shouk, also appears across the investigation: at Zamzam displacement camp during the RSF’s April 2025 assault, then around el-Fasher during its takeover six months later.

His appearances connect two offensives under the same regional command, but they do not establish his responsibility for a specific sexual assault.

Another officer appears on opposing sides of the war.

Abuaqla Mohamed Ahmed Alwakil, known as Kaykal, was appointed commander of an RSF division in Wad Madani on December 19, 2023, according to an RSF announcement cited by CIR.

Investigators verified him at a former army base there on December 24. The same day, the Strategic Initiative for Women in the Horn of Africa documented the rape of seven women at the city’s Industrial School.

The following day, RSF captain Samar Ibrahim Tirab appeared about 750 metres from the school, dismissing reports of rape and looting as lies.

In October 2024, Kaykal defected to the army’s side. When army and allied forces recaptured Wad Madani in January 2025, CIR verified him in the city and nearby Wad al-Mehidi, now commanding the Sudan Shield Forces.

The United Nations human rights office reported that Sudan Shield fighters abducted 13 women and a man from Tayba camp on January 10. Human Rights Watch separately recorded witnesses identifying attackers as Kaykal’s forces. Radio Dabanga reported allegations of rape by the group in Tayba and other settlements.

In Gezira, southeast of Khartoum, CIR also examined abuses against Kanabi communities, historically marginalised settlements made up of descendants of migrant agricultural workers. These communities faced attacks amid accusations of supporting the RSF.

Verified footage from Hantoub Bridge shows fighters beating and sexually degrading a detained man before pushing him off the bridge. CIR identified insignia associated with the army-allied Baraa Bin Malik Brigade, General Intelligence Service and Special Mission Forces.

The most senior army officer CIR placed in Wad Madani during the recapture was Major-General Abdelmoneim Abdelbasit Mohamed, commander of the Sennar axis, identified on January 12, 2025.

His presence is part of CIR’s assessment of command structures, but it does not establish that he directed the filmed attack.

Al Jazeera contacted the RSF and the Sudanese Armed Forces to ask for a response to the findings laid out in this article, but received no response.

Both the RSF and the Sudanese Armed Forces have previously denied allegations of sexual violence by their personnel.

On October 26, Britain imposed sanctions on 15 senior commanders from Sudan’s rival forces over suspected atrocities, including conflict-related sexual violence.

The measures include asset freezes and travel bans. Among those named were Abu Jalak and Al-Nour Ahmed Adam, known as al-Qubba, whom the UK Foreign Office linked to the siege and assault on el-Fasher.

The UK government said the announcement followed CIR reporting on sexual violence and starvation. It also pledged 5 million pounds ($6.7m) for survivors, including healthcare and psychosocial support, and a further 10 million pounds ($13.4m) for humanitarian assistance.

The 15 sanctions designations are a separate list from the 25 commanders cited in CIR’s report, and sanctions do not equate to criminal convictions.

CIR says it has reasonable grounds to believe the commanders identified were directly or indirectly responsible for sexual violence. It also explicitly states that data limitations prevent it from attributing individual responsibility for specific incidents.

Presence, rank and repeated appearances can guide further investigation; but they cannot alone establish criminal guilt. A command-responsibility case would also require evidence about effective control, knowledge and failures to take necessary measures to prevent, repress or report crimes.

For survivors, stigma, insecurity and inaccessible services still obstruct both treatment and testimony. The investigation preserves another source of evidence: the images fighters recorded themselves.

articles.title: Halloween candy favorites could leave adults with cracked teeth and far worse, says dentist
articles.summary: Dr. Marc Lazare tells Fox News Digital which Halloween candy poses the biggest risks to dental crowns, fillings and enamel — and shares his top treat pick.
articles.body: Cavities aren't the only Halloween candy hazard — many sweets can cause a fright to teeth and dental work even in adults, a dentist warns. Hard sweets can crack a tooth, while sticky treats can pull out dental work, potentially turning a trick-or-treat haul into an expensive dental visit, according to Dr. Marc Lazare, a New York City dentist who has practiced for nearly 30 years and focuses on biomimetic dentistry. But Lazare isn't trying to spook people. YOUR FAVORITE GROCERY AND SNACK ITEMS MAY HAVE DISAPPEARED FROM STORE SHELVES IN 2026 "I'm never going to be the dentist who says, 'Don't enjoy Halloween. Don't have candy,'" he told Fox News Digital. "I love Halloween." It's all about moderation, he said. As a dentist, he said he evaluates candy by how it could damage teeth: "Can it harm the enamel? Can it contribute to decay and cavities? Can it pull out a filling or a crown? Can it crack a tooth?" People with fillings, posts, crowns, existing cracks or teeth weakened by grinding are particularly vulnerable, he noted. Hard sweets can force people to crunch down, which may crack or split a tooth, especially one that has already been restored, Lazare said. GEN Z EATS NEARLY TWICE AS MANY SNACKS AS BOOMERS, WITH EXPERTS WARNING THEY'RE REPLACING REAL MEALS "Anything where you have to force a crunch is not good," he said. Super-sticky candies and caramels can cling to teeth and pull out fillings or crowns. Chewy sweets can get stuck between teeth, prolonging sugar exposure and what Lazare called an "acid attack." Sour candy can also expose enamel to acid, he warned. He recommended avoiding snacking throughout the day to help limit acid exposure. BEST FOODS FOR REDUCING DANGEROUS BELLY FAT AND PROTECTING HEART HEALTH Candy isn't the only Halloween treat that can haunt your teeth, Lazare noted. While raisins are often seen as a healthier alternative for trick-or-treaters, they can stick to teeth and also contribute to prolonged acid exposure. "Raisins are probably one of the worst things you can have for your teeth," he said. Lazare said his treat recommendation would be chocolate, which melts and dissolves quickly. Dark chocolate is best, he said, because it tends to be lower in sugar than other candy, but beware of fillings like raisins and toffee in that chocolate. If you do indulge in some Halloween candy, Lazare said, some easy tips can help mitigate the damage. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Rinse with water and wait about an hour before brushing because acid can temporarily soften tooth enamel and brushing immediately may increase wear. Then maintain your regular brushing and flossing routine. Sugar-free gum can also help clear food from teeth and get saliva flowing, Lazare said. If a crown or other restoration comes out, "don't panic," he said. "Stop chewing on that side, save any crown or restoration that comes off, and contact your dentist promptly. Never try to reattach it with household glue." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Anyone experiencing severe pain, swelling or significant bleeding should "seek urgent dental care," he said. Some restorations may be reusable, depending on their condition. The main goal, Lazare said, is prevention, a central tenet of his biomimetic approach, which focuses on preserving natural tooth structure for the long term. articles.title: Common developmental condition linked to higher risk of Parkinson's-related disorders
articles.summary: Older adults with autism were diagnosed with parkinsonism at more than double the rate of the general population, a study of 57 million Americans found.
articles.body: Older adults diagnosed with autism face a significantly higher risk of developing Parkinson’s disease-related movement disorders compared to the general population, according to a large new study published in the journal Autism. Researchers analyzed Medicare and Medicaid claims data covering nearly 57 million Americans aged 45 and older between 2017 and 2019. Individuals on the spectrum, as well as those with intellectual disabilities, were diagnosed with parkinsonism at much higher rates than those without autism. HOW EATING HABITS COULD INFLUENCE PARKINSON’S DISEASE RISK, ACCORDING TO EXPERTS Parkinsonism refers to a range of neurological conditions characterized by certain movement symptoms, including tremors, muscle rigidity, balance difficulties and slowed voluntary movement, according to the Parkinson’s Foundation. While earlier research suggested an overlap between autism and motor decline later in life, it was unclear whether those problems stemmed from the condition or from antipsychotic medications, which are widely known to trigger Parkinson’s-like symptoms as a secondary side effect. To determine whether medications explained the link, researchers excluded people who took antipsychotics from the analysis. They still found higher rates of Parkinson’s-related diagnoses in neurodivergent populations. In the general population control group, the prevalence of parkinsonism was roughly 1.57%. The prevalence rose to 3.83% among adults with autism alone, 4.32% for those with an intellectual disability alone, and 4.86% among individuals diagnosed with both autism and an intellectual disability. PARKINSON’S PATIENT’S YEARS-LONG TREMOR VANISHES WITHIN MINUTES OF NEW ULTRASOUND TREATMENT "A critically important new contribution of this study is increased incidence rates of parkinsonism for autistic people in middle and older adulthood, which suggests that these cases aren’t simply a byproduct of lifelong motor challenges," Greg Wallace, lead author and a professor in the Department of Speech, Language and Hearing Sciences at The George Washington University in Washington, D.C., said in a press release. The study represents the first time scientists have tracked the incidence rate, or the risk of newly emerging cases over time, among older autistic individuals. "It is therefore important for clinicians to establish clear baselines of motor skills and challenges during adulthood that can be tracked over time," Wallace added. Dr. Lee Murray, a neurologist based in Jackson, Tennessee, said this study clarifies previous research that suggested patients with autism are at a higher risk of having Parkinson's. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "This study takes into account the use of antipsychotic medications that can cause a Parkinson's look (resting tremor, stiffness, shuffled gait, stooped posture, softened voice), which is a different pathology than stereotypical or idiopathic Parkinson's disease," Murray, who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital. "This study showed patients with autism that was associated with intellectual disability seem to have the greatest association with concomitant Parkinson's." The neurologist cautioned that autism encompasses a wide range of symptoms and severity, so the findings don't mean that people with milder cases face a significantly higher risk of Parkinson’s disease. "It certainly is an interesting correlation, although it does not imply that someone with autism is certain to develop Parkinson's," Murray added. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "From a clinical perspective, it's helpful to review medications with the autistic patient's physicians and, if possible, try to avoid medications that may cause a Parkinson's appearance." Despite the scope of the data, the authors noted several key limitations of using insurance records. The investigation relied on billing and diagnostic codes submitted through Medicare and Medicaid, which can contain errors or reflect differences in how clinics and medical providers diagnose conditions. The reliance on claims data also means researchers could not assess the severity of individual motor symptoms or examine the role of lifestyle factors, genetics and family history, they noted. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Additionally, the data only captured adults who were enrolled in public insurance programs, potentially leaving out older individuals who rely strictly on private health insurance. "Patients with autism can have atypical movements that can be misdiagnosed as Parkinson's if the examiner is not accustomed to diagnosing it." Because people on the autism spectrum may already struggle with coordination, repetitive behaviors or executive functioning challenges, experts say early indicators of Parkinson’s disease can be missed or mistaken, potentially delaying essential care. The researchers emphasized the need for physicians, long-term care facilities and family caregivers to closely monitor older autistic patients for motor decline so interventions can begin as early as possible.

articles.title: Doctor Shares 3 Lifestyle Habits to Reduce Breast Cancer Risk
articles.summary: You may not have control over your genes, but lifestyle factors are ones you can change. Focus on these three lifestyle habits to reduce your risk for cancer.
articles.body: Everyone’s personal risk for cancer will be different, based on their genetics, family history and environmental exposures. While you can’t change your genes, lifestyle factors are ones that you do generally have more control over. And practicing certain healthy lifestyle habits can reduce your risk for breast cancer (and cancer in general), regardless of your genes. Expert Tip of the Day: Focus on These Lifestyle Habits to Reduce Your Risk for Cancer Here are the top three lifestyle habits to focus on for cancer prevention, according to Dr. Jennifer Litton, professor of breast medical oncology and chief clinical research officer at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center: Eat a healthy diet that’s low in ultraprocessed foodsGet regular physical activityReduce or cut out tobacco and alcohol Why It Matters Simple lifestyle habits like these can have a big impact on your risk for cancer. And, for people who’ve had cancer in the past, habits like these can also make it less likely the cancer will come back, Dr. Julia Brockway-Marchello, a breast oncologist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, told TODAY.com previously. Healthy eating is the first big one to prioritize, which Litton describes to TODAY.com as “eating a well-balanced diet that is low in super-processed foods.” There’s no single specific diet that’s perfect for everyone, but experts generally recommend aiming to incorporate more whole, plant-based foods while limiting processed foods, especially processed meat and sugary packaged products. And oncologists told TODAY.com previously that they typically gravitate towards a Mediterranean style of eating. When it comes to exercise, don’t feel like you need to go all-in immediately, Litton says. “Don’t wait for perfect. If you can do five minutes here, do that,” she says. “That’s better than doing nothing. Fit it in where you can.” Regular physical activity helps maintain a healthy body weight, boosts cardiovascular health and can support bone health as you age. Finally, if you smoke or drink alcohol, consider quitting or significantly reducing your intake. Tobacco use increases your risk for multiple types of cancer, including breast cancer. “If there’s any single health choice one can make, it’s to not smoke at all, or if you did smoke, to quit,” Dr. Suneel Kamath, medical oncologist at the Cleveland Clinic, told TODAY.com previously. “I don’t think there’s anything healthier, in terms of a behavior choice that you can make.” And, when it comes to alcohol, experts now agree that there’s no amount of drinking that’s considered safe. That doesn’t mean you need to completely quit drinking, but you should recognize that every drink contributes to a real increased risk for cancer, including breast cancer. Other Ways to Reduce Cancer Risk Healthy eating, regular exercise and reducing tobacco and alcohol intake are three of the most significant ways you can reduce your risk for breast cancer and cancer in general. Experts previously also recommended that you: Wear sunscreen regularlyDevelop healthy ways to manage stressDon’t rely on supplementsAsk about your family’s health history Smart habits like these can help make cancer less likely and help you stay on top of your overall health, too. TODAY’s Expert Tip of the Day series is all about simple strategies to make life a little easier. Every Monday through Friday, different qualified experts share their best advice on diet, fitness, heart health, mental wellness and more.

articles.title: Dylan Dreyer Reveals the Ab Workout That Helped Her Get Ready for TODAY’s Halloween Celebration
articles.summary: Dylan Dreyer showed off her abs as Jeannie for TODAY’s Halloween show. She shares her workout, diet and the childhood advice from her dad behind her six-pack.
articles.body: Dylan Dreyer’s six-pack started with a piece of advice from her dad. For TODAY’s annual Halloween extravaganza on Oct. 30, the co-anchor transformed into Jeannie from the classic sitcom “I Dream of Jeannie,” complete with a wig, a stunning wardrobe and a midriff-baring top that put her toned midsection center stage. “I have always, except for when I was pregnant, had a six-pack,” Dylan tells TODAY.com. “And it’s literally because when I was younger, my dad always said to me, ‘Tighten your stomach.’” So she did, and she never stopped. Keeping her core tight as she went about her day became second nature, a built-in workout decades before it ever had a national audience. “It’s not like I’m sitting there doing 1,000 sit-ups a day to get my stomach in shape,” she says. (One caveat for anyone tempted to copy her: Physical therapists warn that constantly sucking in your stomach can lead to “hourglass syndrome,” a pattern in which the diaphragm can’t fully expand, causing shallow breathing, back pain and extra pressure on the pelvic floor.) Still, Dylan didn’t leave the big reveal to chance. “I have stepped up my game a little bit in the last couple weeks because I knew this costume was coming,” she says. Her secret weapon is the Soto Method, a program created by trainer Hilary Hoffman. The name stands for “60 on, 10 on:” Each block opens with a 60-second isometric hold, followed by 10 moves meant to push the muscles to failure. Dylan’s go-to routine ends with a five-minute core finisher designed to leave the muscles burning. “You really feel it afterward,” she says. The day before the show, she even fit in bonus reps: a quick core circuit in her dressing room, followed by a second workout. She also cut back on sweets in the weeks leading up to the big day, though she didn’t give them up entirely. Dylan kept a bowl of candy corn around and allowed herself a piece when she walked by. Meal timing was already on her side: Dylan is mindful about when she eats, typically finishing dinner around 5:30 p.m. and not eating again until her yogurt the next morning. The mom of three boys gets in some extra movement by taking her sons and the family dog on a long walk after dinner. The extra workouts and skipped sweets aren’t permanent. Dylan plans to return to her usual routine once Halloween wraps, and Friday night might call for Chinese food. The six-pack may grab the headlines, but Dylan saves her biggest praise for the people who turned her into Jeannie. “The wardrobe team is unbelievable,” she says.

articles.title: We Asked Dietitians Their Favorite Halloween Candy and This Was the No. 1 Brand
articles.summary: Candy can be part of a healthy diet — especially if it’s part of celebrating Halloween fun. Here’s how dietitians think about candy and their favorites to eat.
articles.body: With Halloween just one day away, you may be craving a good scare, but one thing you don’t need to fear is the candy bowl, dietitians say. Chocolate and sugary gummies aren’t exactly nutrient-packed health foods, and they don’t need to be. The only thing candy should be is delicious. And you don’t need to avoid it, dietitians tell TODAY.com, especially if doing so would mean denying yourself a part of a fun holiday tradition like Halloween. Sugary candy, including Halloween candy, can definitely still be part of a mindful, healthy diet, Erin Palinski-Wade, a registered dietitian based in New Jersey, tells TODAY.com. “In fact, trying to avoid it completely usually just makes you crave it more,” she says. And, yes, even dietitians eat candy, says Grace Derocha, a registered dietitian and spokesperson for the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics. “It’s fun, and food can be part of traditions and celebrations,” she explains. Your approach to candy should be “about balance and not perfection,” Derocha adds. How to Fit Candy Into a Healthy Diet When thinking about Halloween or any time of year when treats are part of the season, Derocha suggests leaning on what she calls the three Ps: portion size, being present and taking pleasure. Regarding portion size, take advantage of the fact that Halloween candy typically comes in a smaller “fun size,” Derocha says. “It will satisfy your craving without going overboard because it’s already in that smaller packaging,” she explains. Next, take a moment to be mindful and present when eating your chosen candy. “Slow down and really taste it,” Derocha says, “so that you can enjoy that chocolatey or sweet moment of that candy.” And finally, know that food should be pleasurable, especially if it’s a meaningful part of a celebration like Halloween festivities. “I like to think of candy as part of the fun of the season,” Palinski-Wade says. “(It’s) something to be enjoyed mindfully, not something to feel guilty about.” Caroline Susie, a registered dietitian based in Dallas, agrees that “all foods fit.” She likes to pair candy with a meal containing fiber and protein, which “helps blunt blood sugar spikes and makes it a more satisfying experience,” she explains. But, ultimately, no single food defines a “healthy” diet, Susie says. “What matters most is the dietary pattern.” That should include a variety of nutrient-dense foods, “while leaving space for enjoyment and flexibility,” she explains. “Candy can absolutely fit into that picture without guilt.” Dietitians’ Favorite Halloween Candy Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups Dessert is a daily habit for Whitney Linsenmeyer, Ph.D, registered dietitian, and she frequently chooses dark chocolate. When it comes to Halloween candy, she tells TODAY.com that her decision is purely guided by taste. When she’s feeling “savory and salty,” she chooses a Reese’s. In fact, Reese’s items were a consistent favorite across the dietitians TODAY.com polled. The classic peanut butter cups are Susie’s favorite, and Derocha is partial to the mini cups. Meanwhile, registered dietitian Natalie Rizzo, who is also the nutrition editor at TODAY, gravitates to Reese’s Pieces. “I have always been more of a savory person, so if I could choose a dessert, it would always be peanut-butter flavored,” Rizzo says. Skittles Palinski-Wade is a big fan of foods that combine sweet and sour tastes, so she likes the combination of tangy flavors found in candies like Skittles and Starbursts. Peanut M&Ms Another of Derocha’s top picks is M&Ms — specifically the peanut variety — for the satisfying combination of textures. “I like the crunch from the peanut, I like the chocolateyness, and then the sugary coating,” she says. “It has all the things!” And, thanks to the peanut, there is a little bit of fat and protein in this candy, Derocha notes. Mini Snickers Derocha also loves the mini Snickers bars and turns finding them into a game with her family. Each of the small candies has a letter of the word Snickers on the packaging, and her kids “know that’s one of my favorites, so they try to spell Snickers for me,” she explains. “And then my thing is that I get a Snickers a week.” It’s fun to find all the letters (and to see what words the family can spell as they run out of certain letters), she says, “but it also does give me some perspective on the amount.” York Peppermint Patties When Linsenmeyer is the mood for something “light and zesty,” she likes to reach for minty candies, like York Peppermint Patties or Junior Mints. Malted Milk Balls This one is all about nostalgia for Palinski-Wade. “Malted milk balls always remind me of my own Nana who always had a stash of these on hand whenever we came over to visit,” she says. Smarties “They’re sweet and tart at the same time, without being overly sweet like some of the other like pure sugar candies,” Derocha says of this favorite. Plus, her kids aren’t fans of Smarties, so she gets to have theirs.

articles.title: Moldy food isn't always dangerous, expert says: 'Spit it out and move on with your day'
articles.summary: Professor Brian Labus, Ph.D., tells Fox News Digital why firmness matters when deciding whether to cut mold off food and which items like bread and berries should be tossed.
articles.body: Finding a moldy piece of produce creates a familiar kitchen gamble, but the risk depends on what's growing and what it's growing on, experts say. A recent survey out of Germany found that nearly one in three people cut mold off food before eating the rest, a habit that may not remove all toxins. Fewer than half of respondents knew that cooking or baking does not destroy mycotoxins, which are produced by certain molds and can be invisible in foods. More than a quarter thought heat could destroy them, while another quarter were unsure. SCIENTISTS SAY YOU'VE BEEN THROWING AWAY PERFECTLY GOOD MEAT BECAUSE OF ONE COMMON MISTAKE The survey, which was conducted by Germany's Federal Institute for Risk Assessment, measured reported habits and knowledge, not toxin levels in food or illness. The report highlighted the limits of relying on sight to judge food safety. "Visible mold is reliably recognized and triggers intuitive avoidance," the authors wrote. "But this instinct does not work when food contains toxins without visible mold." But what to do about moldy food really depends on the item, according to Brian Labus, an infectious disease epidemiologist and associate professor at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas School of Public Health. "Those things are gross, but they're not the kind of thing that's going to make you sick." People often confuse ordinary spoilage with the kinds of germs that cause foodborne illness, he told Fox News Digital. GREEN BANANAS AREN'T NECESSARILY BAD — EXPERTS EXPLAIN THE HIDDEN HEALTH PERK "Most of the stuff that we're talking about, especially with fruits and vegetables, it's not going to be something that's going to cause a foodborne illness," Labus said. "Those things are gross, but they're not the kind of thing that's going to make you sick." Firmness is a useful guide when deciding what to do with visible mold, Labus said. On a firm fruit such as an apple, he said, mold may remain near the surface, so a person can cut around the affected area. On soft, wet foods, mold can spread more easily through the food. MOLD COULD BE LURKING IN YOUR COFFEE MAKER AS EXPERT REVEALS 5 WAYS TO KEEP IT CLEAN If lettuce or other produce has become mushy, he said, it should be thrown away. With berries, discard any pieces with visible mold or soft spots, Labus said. Other berries that remain intact and show no signs of mold can be washed and eaten. U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) guidance similarly advises throwing out moldy fruit and any pieces touching it, then washing the rest if they show no mold and are not overly mushy. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Bread is different, Labus said, because mold can grow into the loaf. If mold appears on a slice, he recommends throwing out the bread rather than removing only the visibly affected part. Germany's risk assessment agency recommends discarding moldy, water-rich produce. "It's not like you need to run to the doctor or anything like that. Spit it out and move on with your day." Moldy jam or jelly should also be discarded, Labus said. Some molds can trigger allergic reactions, and certain molds produce mycotoxins, according to the USDA. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ But if you accidentally eat something moldy, Labus said not to panic. "It's not like you need to run to the doctor or anything like that," he said. "Spit it out and move on with your day." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES People with mold allergies should avoid taking chances with moldy food, while those who are immunocompromised should be especially cautious with food handling overall, Labus said. Labus also recommends keeping food refrigerated and buying only what you'll use soon — rather than stocking up on a wholesale-size container of berries. For example, he said, using the same knife on raw chicken and then on vegetables without washing it can spread illness-causing germs.

articles.title: Sikar man killed after argument, police launch probe
articles.summary: Sikar: 35-year-old Surendra killed after argument at Devas village tailor shop; accused Ashok Kumar stabbed him with scissors, police probe and search underway.
articles.body: Jhunjhunu: A 35-year-old man was murdered after an argument at Devas village in Fatehpur area of Sikar Friday.The deceased was identified as Surendra.Fatehpur police station officer Mahendra Kumar said that Surendra had an argument at a tailor shop in Devas village.During the dispute, Ashok Kumar stabbed Surendra in the stomach with scissors and fled after the incident.Later, villagers informed Sadar police station.Police took Surendra to the Trauma Centre of govt sub-district hospital in Fatehpur, where doctors declared him dead.Police have launched an investigation from a murder angle and launched a search for the accused.The reason for the argument and the entire sequence behind the incident n also being investigated.
